concept.name: Proof of work
concept.definition: Proof of work (PoW) is a Sybil-resistance and block-author-selection mechanism in which miners compete to find a nonce that makes a block's hash fall below a difficulty target, expending real-world computation; the chain with the most accumulated work is treated as canonical.
concept.intuition: Miners burn electricity on a lottery; the winning ticket lets them write the next page of the ledger, and cheating would require out-computing the whole honest network.
concept.mechanics: Miners repeatedly hash a candidate block header with different nonces until the hash meets the target set by the difficulty parameter; difficulty retargets to keep average block time constant. Validity is cheap to verify but expensive to produce, and the longest (most-work) chain rule resolves forks.
concept.formula: Find nonce n such that H(block_header(n)) <= T, where T = target set by difficulty (lower T = harder); probability per hash ≈ T / 2^256 (SHA-256).
concept.failure_modes: An attacker controlling a majority of hash rate can double-spend by mining a private chain that outpaces the honest one; mining-pool centralization and hardware/energy concentration erode the security model.
concept.misconceptions: PoW does not 'solve a useful puzzle' — the computation is deliberately useless work whose only purpose is to be costly. High hash rate secures history but does not increase transaction throughput.
concept.example: In Bitcoin, miners increment a nonce until the block hash has the required number of leading zero bits; at ~10-minute block targets, an attacker trying to reverse a 6-block-deep transaction must redo that work and then outpace all honest miners, an economically prohibitive task.

citations.source: Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (whitepaper)
